To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we have: (i) calculated the neutrino beam fluxes and composition at NOMAD, and (ii) estimated the uncertainty of the calculations.
the flux and composition at the NOMAD detector have been determined to within 10% and that the νe/ νμ flux ratio is predicted with an accuracy of 4.2% (7%) at the 1 GeV (3 GeV) neutrino energy.
the flux of neutrinos produced at CERN's West Area Neutrinos Facility is well understood, with uncertainties of 8% for the νμ and ν e, 10% for the ν μ, and of 12% for the ν e.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the calculation of neutrino flux in the West Area Neutron Beam used by the NOMAD experiment in its search for the ν μ → ν e oscillation.
the calculation and prediction of the neutrino fluxes produced by the West Area Nevento beam.
the study of the production, transport and detection of neutrino beams.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the fluxes of all neutrinos at the NOMAD detector are known with a total uncertainty of 8%, with an energy-dependent uncertainty ranging from 3.6% to 8.5% and a total uncertainty on the ratio of νe to νμ of 4.2%.
the fluxes and composition are predicted to a precision of about 8%.
the fluxes of neutrinos produced by the WA neutrino beam and reaching the NOMAD detector are predicted with a total uncertainty of 8% for all neutrinos, 10% on ν μ and ν e, and 12.5% on ν e.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

we have been able to predict with a precision of a few per cent the neutrino fluxes at NOMAD and the neutrino energy spectrum, and that we have been successful in predicting the composition of the beam, which is a key ingredient to the understanding of the νμ→ντ oscillation search.

we can predict the neutrino fluxes at the NOMAD detector with a precision better than 10%, and that the flux of the neutrino flavour of interest (νe) can be predicted with a precision better then 6% in most of the energy range.
the neutrino beam fluxes and composition are predicted with an accuracy sufficient for NOMAD to carry out the search for neutrino mass and mixing proposed in the NOMAD Letter of Intent.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the fluxes of the neutrinos produced by the West Area Neutron Beam at CERN are well understood.
a detailed simulation of the neutrino beam line is essential for a precise prediction of the neutrino fluxes at the NOMAD experiment.
a precise knowledge of the neutrino beam is essential in the search for neutrino mass differences.
